claims.text: The initial alloy is AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy.
The as-cast alloy has a fine, regular lamellar microstructure of alternating soft fcc and hard B2 phases.
The initial alloy exhibits catastrophic interfacial cracking and low ductility in room-temperature uniaxial tension.
Hydrostatic pressure above 20 GPa can induce an fcc-to-hcp polymorphic transition in a high-entropy alloy.
A pressure threshold above 20 GPa is applicable to polymorphic transformation or dense stacking-fault formation in AlCoCrFeNi2.1.
Combining pressure above 20 GPa with 400–600°C will make the proposed transformation kinetically accessible in AlCoCrFeNi2.1.
The 400–600°C treatment window is below the eutectic reaction temperature and will preserve the alloy's phase constitution.
The treatment can alter the microstructure without changing the bulk alloy composition.
High pressure lowers or overcomes the kinetic barrier to an fcc-to-hcp transition.
Low stacking-fault energy permits local stacking faults that facilitate pressure-induced fcc-to-hcp transformation.
Extreme-pressure treatment will create an fcc-to-hcp transition or a high density of stacking faults within the fcc lamellae of AlCoCrFeNi2.1.
The pressure-induced defects or transition will disrupt continuous planar lamellae and produce a patterned, interlocking, non-continuous interface.
Non-planar, non-continuous interfaces will reduce interfacial stress concentration and impede crack propagation.
The patterned two-phase structure will promote dislocation storage and work hardening.
The treatment will change fracture from catastrophic interfacial cracking to quasi-cleavage or ductile-dimple fracture.
The treatment will significantly increase uniform elongation while maintaining or increasing yield strength.
Conventional HIP below 2 GPa heals porosity but cannot generate the proposed transition or stacking-fault density and therefore cannot alter lamellar continuity or arrest interfacial cracks.
Excessive treatment temperature may coarsen or dissolve the eutectic structure and negate its composite effect.

contradictions.description: The main hypothesis assigns a possible localized polymorphic transition to the B2 phase, whereas the structural mediator and mechanism specify an fcc-to-hcp transition within the fcc lamellae. The phase undergoing the proposed polymorphic transition is therefore inconsistent.
